summary_en: This paper presents a dual-parameter photoacoustic system that combines conventional photoacoustic absorption imaging with photoacoustic viscoelasticity imaging. Optical-absorption contrast estimates melanoma morphology and lesion thickness, while phase delay in intensity-modulated photoacoustic signals provides complementary viscoelastic information. Phantom tests and longitudinal in-vivo melanoma experiments show that the two contrast channels capture distinct structural and mechanical properties. Because the contribution introduces a substantive acoustic-optical image-formation and characterization method rather than downstream classification alone, it is a core repository addition.
